s1.syndrome_frame: intermittent pelvic pain and gross hematuria with ureteral obstruction
salient_findings: tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
key_facts: renal ultrasound and cystoscopy showed no abnormalities
tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter
urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy were negative for malignancy
slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis
subtle thickening of the right ureter
no evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Ureteral transitional cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common ureteral tumor, consistent with patient's age and smoking history

shortlist.label: Ureteral fibroepithelial polyp
shortlist.why_kept: benign tumor, could cause ureteral obstruction and hematuria

shortlist.label: Ureteral leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: benign tumor, possible cause of ureteral obstruction and pelvic pain

shortlist.label: Ureteral squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: less common ureteral tumor, but possible given patient's age and smoking history

shortlist.label: Ureteral inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rare tumor, but could cause ureteral obstruction and hematuria, and patient has history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a pedunculated ureteral tumor with a vulnerable surface and the absence of malignancy on urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy are consistent with a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp, which is a benign tumor

rejected.label: Ureteral polyp
rejected.why: While a ureteral polyp could explain some symptoms, the specific characteristics of the tumor, such as being pedunculated and having a vulnerable surface, are more typical of a fibroepithelial polyp
